topic: Energy Bands: Conductors, Insulators and Semiconductors
title: Why Does Copper Conduct? Explained Simply | PUC, CBSE and ISC
description:
Aarav cuts open an old charger cable: shiny copper inside, soft plastic outside. Both are full of electrons, so why does only the copper carry current? And why does the silicon in his phone conduct only sometimes? The answer is energy bands. We picture a building with a packed ground floor (the valence band), an empty upper floor (the conduction band) and a jump between them (the forbidden energy gap, Eg), then sort solids into conductors (bands overlap), insulators (diamond, gap 5.4 eV) and semiconductors (silicon 1.1 eV, germanium about 0.7 eV).

On a live breadboard a heater warms a copper wire and then a piece of pure silicon while the oscilloscope tracks the current: the metal's current drops a little, the silicon's current climbs as electrons jump the gap and leave holes behind. Worked example: the longest wavelength of light that can lift an electron across silicon's gap (about 1130 nm, infrared) and the 1240 / Eg shortcut. Then the exam trap, where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a fact card to screenshot.

This is Episode 38 of PUC Electronics. Karnataka I PUC Electronics Ch 6: Semiconductors, Diodes and Applications of Diodes | NCERT/CBSE Class 12 Physics Ch 14: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits | ISC Class 12 Physics: Electronic Devices (energy bands in conductors, semiconductors and insulators).
